-- Reads `name` inside the confined `notes` directory.
-- None if the file is missing or unreadable, or if the name is not a plain
-- file name (path separators, "..", absolute paths, empty names, NUL bytes).
read_note(name: str) -> str? uses fs =
  post out == None or name.char_count() > 0
  ex read_note("../secret") == None
  ex read_note("/etc/passwd") == None
  ex read_note("a/../../b") == None
  ex read_note("") == None
  if name.char_count() == 0 or name == "." or name == ".."
    return None
  for c in name.chars()
    if c == "/" or c == "\\"
      return None
  var found: str? = None
  with fs = fs.sub("notes")
    found = fs.read(name) else None
  found

-- Text of the first name in `names` that can be read from `notes`, or "" if none can.
-- A readable empty file counts as readable, and its empty text is the result.
first_readable(names: List[str]) -> str uses fs =
  post names.len() > 0 or out == ""
  ex first_readable([]) == ""
  ex first_readable(["../secret", "/etc/passwd"]) == ""
  for n in names
    let t = read_note(n)
    if t != None
      return t else ""
  ""

test_first_readable_empty() uses fs =
  assert first_readable([]) == ""

test_first_readable_escape() uses fs =
  assert first_readable(["../secret", "/etc/passwd", "a/../../b"]) == ""
